advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the two `git config --global` calls (helper + useHttpPath) with `|| { echo ...; rc=1; }` (or similar) so a config failure surfaces in the exit status instead of aborting provision_store under `set -e`.
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:27: `set -e`

infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:199-201: `git config --global "credential.${MCP_TICKETS_URL}.helper" \ ...` and `git config --global "credential.${MCP_TICKETS_URL}.useHttpPath" false` — neither is followed by `|| {...}` or `|| true`, unlike the clone (line 182), ensure (line 216), and lock ops (lines 148,158) which all trap their failures
Header comment lines 23-26 promise: 'FAILURE POSTURE IS SOFT ... provision_store still RETURNS non-zero when a step failed so the failure surfaces ... instead of being silently treated as success'
ABSENCE: the `_GIT_STUB` in tests/unit/test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py answers `config) exit 0 ;;` unconditionally, so no test drives a git-config failure
advisory.finding: The two `git config --global` calls in provision_store are unguarded simple commands under `set -e`; if either fails (unwritable HOME, corrupt ~/.gitconfig) the whole provision_store aborts before the ensure step and before the terminal `provisioning finished` line — violating the documented soft failure posture and giving no honest non-zero return via the normal path.
scenarios: Container/volume with an unwritable or read-only HOME, or a pre-existing corrupt ~/.gitconfig, when MCP_TICKETS_PAT is set
Backgrounded run: provision_store dies mid-function, no `provisioning finished` marker, boot continues but the store is never converged and the failure is invisible except for git's own stderr
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap each `git config --global ...` in `|| { echo "mcp: git credential config failed" >&2; rc=1; }` so the soft-failure contract holds and the ensure step + terminal line still run.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Prevent the stale-break path from clearing a directory a LIVE peer is still cloning into (heartbeat/refresh the lock timestamp during the clone, or size MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_STALE strictly above the worst-case clone time and document it).
evidence: Shared mutable resource: the persistent volume store dir and its lock — `reclone_lock_path() { printf '%s' "$(tracker_dir).reclone.lock"; }` (line 100) guarding `git clone ... "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"` (line 182)

≥2 executors: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:86-88 — `restart: always` on the compose service and the autodeploy 2-minute timer start a second container into the same volume; provisioning is backgrounded (line 231 `provision_store &`) so the winner's clone outlives its deploy tick

Interleaving READ: `reclone_lock_is_stale` compares `now - started` against MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_STALE (line 116) where `started` is the lock timestamp written ONCE at acquisition (line 131 `printf '%s\n' "$(date +%s)" > "$tmp"`) and never refreshed — a slow live clone reads as stale

Interleaving WRITE: after breaking (line 148 `rm -f "$lock" ...`) and re-acquiring, the waiter reaches `clear_tracker_dir` (line 181) → `(cd "$dir" && rm -rf ./.[!.]* ./* ...)` (line 75), deleting the directory the peer's `git clone` (line 182) is still writing into

Guard does NOT cover this: the double-check `if store_head_resolves` (line 175) only returns early when the peer's clone has COMPLETED (HEAD resolves); a still-in-progress clone leaves HEAD unresolvable, so the waiter proceeds to clear — a guard that detects the racy condition (old lock) and proceeds anyway

Concrete harm: corrupted/partial store — the live peer's clone is destroyed mid-flight, producing exactly the orphaned-objects / dangling-HEAD poisoned volume described in infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:202-206, i.e. lost work plus a re-poisoned store
advisory.finding: The stale-lock break in acquire_reclone_lock breaks a lock still held by a LIVE peer whose clone legitimately exceeds MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_STALE (no heartbeat/timestamp refresh), letting a second container clear the directory out from under an in-progress clone — the same store-corruption harm the change claims to fix.
scenarios: A ~200k-commit clone (explicitly slow, lines 81-82) runs longer than MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_STALE (default 7200s) on a slow network; a peer container restarted by `restart: always` breaks the lock and clears the directory mid-clone.
MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_STALE is tuned down (tests set it to 60) while a real clone is in progress.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the re-clone lock INSIDE the shared volume (e.g. `${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}/.reclone.lock` or a subpath under the mounted tickets dir) so peer containers actually contend on the same lock.
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:100 `reclone_lock_path() { printf '%s' "$(tracker_dir).reclone.lock"; }`
docker-compose.yml:399 `- gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` (only the tickets subdir is the shared volume)
docker-compose.yml:413-415 `(Per-subdir, not one volume over the whole /var/gerrit, so the image's baked binaries are not shadowed.)` — the parent /var/gerrit/site is NOT a shared mount

The lock file path `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets.reclone.lock` is a sibling of, not inside, the mounted volume, so it lands on the container's ephemeral writable layer and is not shared between containers.
advisory.finding: The cross-container re-clone lock is created OUTSIDE the shared volume. `reclone_lock_path` resolves to `$(tracker_dir).reclone.lock` = `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets.reclone.lock`, a sibling of the tracker dir. Only `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` is mounted as the shared named volume `gerrit_mcp_tickets`; the parent `/var/gerrit/site` is per-subdir, not a single shared mount. So the lock sits on each container's ephemeral layer and is NOT visible to peer containers — the cross-container serialization the change is built to provide does not actually hold, and the clear-out-from-under-a-peer interleave remains possible.
scenarios: Blue/green overlap or a `restart: always` restart racing an autodeploy tick: two containers both see HEAD unresolvable, each takes its own private (non-shared) lock, both clear and clone the same shared volume, one clearing the directory the other is mid-clone into — the exact poisoning this change exists to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Make the lock path a child of the mounted volume, e.g. `reclone_lock_path() { printf '%s' "$(tracker_dir)/../mcp-tickets.reclone.lock"; }` is still outside; prefer a locked subdir under a shared mount, or add a dedicated shared volume for the lock. Since the tracker dir itself is cleared during re-clone, use a lock directory that survives the clear and is on the shared mount (e.g. a sibling path that is also a mounted named volume).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the threading.Timer-based peer handoff in test_a_peer_finishing_the_clone_while_we_wait... with a deterministic mechanism (e.g. have the git-stub rev-parse block until a marker the test writes, or gate the lock-release on an observed poll) so the double-check is exercised without relying on wall-clock timing.
evidence: timer = threading.Timer(2.0, peer_finishes)
env={"MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_POLL": "1", "MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_WAIT": "30"}

peer_finishes touches state/head-resolves and unlinks the lock — coordination between it and the subprocess's wait loop is governed only by the 2.0s timer vs the 1s poll interval, with no barrier/pipe/marker the subprocess waits on
advisory.finding: The concurrency test for the double-checked re-probe synchronizes the peer's clone-completion with a wall-clock `threading.Timer(2.0)` racing the subprocess's 1s poll loop, rather than a deterministic barrier/marker handoff; its primary cross-process synchronization is timing-based.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 273 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug d467-e2fc-fd64-49ae has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan d467-e2fc-fd64-49ae` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review d467-e2fc-fd64-49ae` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan d467-e2fc-fd64-49ae --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Provide an orchestration-visible signal (or documented ops check) for a persistently failed background provision, since /health is intentionally decoupled from store readiness.
evidence: infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:231-232 `provision_store &` then `exec "$@"`

docker-compose.yml:402-407 healthcheck hits `/health`, which answers before/independently of the store existing (script comment lines 13-14: `/health never answered` is the failure being avoided, so /health is intentionally decoupled from store readiness)

No compose-level or healthcheck-level signal reflects a persistently failed provision; the failure surfaces only in journald logs (soft-failure posture is by design, but there is no drift/alerting hook).
dropped.finding: The `--provision-only` synchronous path runs under `set -e` and calls `provision_store` whose final `return "$rc"` may be non-zero; combined with the tests relying on non-zero exit, this is intended — but the container path backgrounds `provision_store &` then `exec "$@"`, so a provisioning failure is only visible in logs, never in the container's health or exit status. A permanently-failing clone (bad/expired PAT) leaves the server up serving `store_uninitialized` indefinitely with no surfaced signal at the orchestration layer.
scenarios: An expired or wrong-scope MCP_TICKETS_PAT: every boot's background clone fails, the container reports healthy, and MCP tools return store_uninitialized with no orchestration-visible failure until a human reads logs.
